vnodes.title: FIPS-safe aws-lc-rs range is 1.15.2-1.17.2: aws-lc-rs 1.17.3 requires aws-lc-fips-sys ^0.13.16, 1.17.4 ^0.13.17, 1.18.x requires ^0.14
vnodes.summary: crates.io dependency metadata (2026-10-25): only aws-lc-rs 1.15.2..1.17.2 accept aws-lc-fips-sys ^0.13.1 and so can resolve the certified 0.13.11 (AWS-LC FIPS 3.1.0, CMVP #5298/#5314). 0.14.0-0.14.3 exist (0.14.3 on 2026-10-12) for aws-lc-rs 1.18. An upgrade to 1.18 silently leaves the certified module; tie it to an AWS-LC 4 certificate.

vnodes.title: CVE-2026-14666 advisory: stale RLS policies persist until another invalidation or session end; CVSS 3.0 AC:H/PR:L, tailored exploitation
vnodes.summary: Long-lived sessions stay exposed after upgrading to 17.11/18.6, so the DB gate must recycle pooled connections after the minor upgrade (and after role DDL), not only check the minor version at startup. Medium severity, not a general RLS bypass.

vnodes.title: Go #81199 PAN-OS resets triggered only by ML-DSA codepoints in signature_algorithms_cert (0x0032), not signature_algorithms; maintainer declined a GODEBUG
vnodes.summary: Narrows the middlebox hazard: rustls may not send signature_algorithms_cert (rustls #3214), so exposure is unproven. Related: #79626, Palo Alto threat ID 58033. Mitigation for our outbound clients is a config option to omit ML-DSA sigalgs.

vnodes.summary: Prior art for the shape-B SDK that the explorer did not survey; evaluate or borrow in spike S1 before building from scratch. Snyk 'type-level security' (2026-06) is context. Maturity and audit status unknown.

vnodes.title: Claw-SWE-Bench is built from SWE-bench-Multilingual and Verified-Mini: the two Rust-tops results are one piece of evidence, likely contaminated
vnodes.summary: Independence of dx.claw-swe-rust-agentic and dx.swebench-multilingual-rust is refuted; per-language n=43 (one instance = 2.3pp).

vnodes.title: nginx 1.31.7 preserves QUIC connections across reload/live upgrade via quic_bpf, but quic_bpf cannot be toggled on reload or disabled during a live upgrade with inherited BPF maps; quic_host_key regenerates per reload
vnodes.summary: Existence proof that zero-drop H3 upgrade is shippable (Linux 5.7+, BPF CID steering), with the cost that per-reload key regeneration invalidates stateless-reset and address-validation tokens.
